headline: Google Home lets any AI agent control your smart devices
summary: Google is rolling out early access to its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, enabling AI agents to securely interact with Google Home devices and access event history.
details: Google Home owners can soon control their smart home devices using any AI agent that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This feature, now in early access, allows agents like Claude, ChatGPT, and Google Antigravity to securely connect with Google Home devices and review event history.

Users will be able to use natural language commands to manage their smart home, such as reviewing camera footage, monitoring activity, controlling devices, and creating custom dashboards. The integration aims to make smart home management more intuitive and accessible through AI.

To set up the connection, users need to create a Google Cloud project, configure it for Home MCP, and then provide these details to their chosen AI agent. The agent will then guide the user through a sign-in and permission granting process.
The system supports all devices within the Google Home ecosystem, including Google Nest products and any 'Works with Google Home' or Matter-compatible devices like smart light bulbs.

Google already utilizes MCP in other services like Google Cloud, data platforms, developer tools, and Google Workspace. The Google Home integration specifically targets consumers experimenting with AI agents for daily tasks.

Access to MCP for Google Home is rolling out starting today and over the coming weeks to subscribers of Google Home Premium Advanced in the U.S. This premium tier costs $20 per month and offers enhanced features like extended video history and detailed notifications.

headline: Anthropic merges Claude chat and Cowork into a single interface
summary: The AI assistant now combines its chat capabilities with document creation and editing features, aiming to compete more directly with tools like Google Docs.
details: Anthropic has announced a significant update to its Claude AI assistant, merging its Claude Cowork functionality directly into the main chat interface. This consolidation aims to streamline the user experience by bringing document creation and editing tools alongside conversational AI.

Previously, users had to switch between different modes or interfaces for chat and document work. Now, Claude will offer a unified experience, allowing users to generate, edit, and refine documents within the same conversation window, similar to how users interact with productivity suites.

This move positions Claude as a more direct competitor to other AI-powered productivity tools, such as Google's Gemini, which also integrates document analysis and creation features. The unified approach seeks to enhance efficiency for users who rely on AI for both information retrieval and content generation.

The updated Claude interface will allow users to create editable documents, suggesting it can handle tasks ranging from drafting emails to generating more complex content. This integration is expected to make Claude a more versatile tool for professionals and creatives alike.

Anthropic's decision to merge these functionalities reflects a growing trend in the AI space towards integrated platforms that offer a broader range of services. By simplifying the user journey, Anthropic hopes to increase engagement and utility for its AI assistant.
